\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The engineering question}

Compression schemes in practice separate into two artifacts: a \emph{decompressor}, shared across all uses and amortized over many files, and a \emph{compressed message}, paid once per file. The pigeonhole principle forbids a scheme that shortens all inputs, but says nothing about how bits are apportioned between these artifacts. A decompressor that knows your data is a Markov chain of order $3$ with specific transition probabilities need not spend message bits describing that structure; a universal decompressor must.

How many bits does universality cost? Equivalently, what is the maximal saving a specialized decompressor could ever deliver? If the answer is a vanishing fraction of the message, specialization is a micro-optimization; if it is an unbounded number of bits, it is a structural win.

\subsection{Codes as distributions}

Fix a finite message set $\Xset$. By Kraft's inequality, uniquely decodable binary codes on $\Xset$ correspond, up to one bit of rounding, to probability distributions $q$ on $\Xset$, the codeword length of $x$ being $-\log_2 q(x)$. We work with idealized (non-integer) lengths, so a \emph{compression scheme} is a distribution $q$ and a \emph{source} is a distribution $p$.

\begin{definition}[Source class]
A \emph{source class} on a finite message set $\Xset$, with parameter set $\Theta$, is a family $\Sclass=\{p_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta}$ of functions $p_\theta:\Xset\to\mathbb{R}$ with $p_\theta(x)\ge0$ and $\sum_{x}p_\theta(x)=1$ for all $\theta$. We write $\ml(x)=\sup_{\theta}p_\theta(x)$ for the \emph{maximum likelihood} of a message.
\end{definition}

The parameter set $\Theta$ is arbitrary---possibly infinite, uncountable, non-compact. We never assume the supremum is attained; all arguments use only that $p_\theta(x)\le\ml(x)$ for all $\theta$, and that $p_\theta(x)\le c$ for all $\theta$ implies $\ml(x)\le c$.

\begin{definition}[Pointwise redundancy and price of universality]
For a scheme $q$, source $p_\theta$ and message $x$ with $q(x)>0$, set $R(q,\theta,x)=\log_2\bigl(p_\theta(x)/q(x)\bigr)$. The \emph{price of universality} of $\Sclass$ is
\[
\price(\Sclass)=\inf_{q}\ \sup_{x}\ \sup_{\theta}\ R(q,\theta,x).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shtarkov sum]
$\displaystyle \Cs(\Sclass)=\sum_{x\in\Xset}\ml(x)=\sum_{x\in\Xset}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}p_\theta(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact minimax identity]\label{thm:shtarkov}
For every nonempty source class $\Sclass$ on a finite message set,
\[
\price(\Sclass)=\log_2\Cs(\Sclass),
\]
attained by the \emph{normalized maximum likelihood} (NML) distribution $q^*(x)=\ml(x)/\Cs(\Sclass)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$q^*$ is a probability distribution by construction, and $\log_2\bigl(p_\theta(x)/q^*(x)\bigr)=\log_2\bigl(p_\theta(x)\Cs/\ml(x)\bigr)\le\log_2\Cs$ for every $\theta,x$, with equality approached at the maximizer; so $q^*$ achieves exactly $\log_2\Cs$. Conversely, if some $q$ had $\sup_{x,\theta}R(q,\theta,x)<\log_2\Cs$, then $q(x)>\ml(x)/\Cs$ for every $x$, and summing gives $1>1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Universality never helps]\label{prop:nonneg}
$\Cs(\Sclass)\ge1$, hence $\price(\Sclass)\ge0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Pick $\theta_0\in\Theta$; then $\Cs\ge\sum_x p_{\theta_0}(x)=1$.
\end{proof}

Everything downstream is an estimate of the single scalar $\Cs$.

\section{Two general tools, and the memoryless class}

\subsection{Sufficient statistics give upper bounds}

\begin{lemma}[Statistic-counting bound]\label{lem:stat}
Let $T:\Xset\to\Sigma$ be a map into a finite set with $T(x)=T(y)\Rightarrow p_\theta(x)=p_\theta(y)$ for all $\theta$. Then $\Cs(\Sclass)\le|\Sigma|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Partition $\Xset$ into the fibers of $T$. On a fiber $F$, $\ml$ is constant, say $v_F$, and for any $\theta$ nearly attaining the supremum, $|F|\,p_\theta(x_F)=\sum_{x\in F}p_\theta(x)\le1$, so $v_F\le1/|F|$. Each fiber contributes $|F|v_F\le1$ to $\Cs$, and there are at most $|\Sigma|$ nonempty fibers.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Type]
For $x\in A^n$ and $a\in A$, let $N_a(x)=\#\{j:x_j=a\}$; the \emph{type} of $x$ is $N(x)=(N_a(x))_{a\in A}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Counts sum to the length]\label{lem:counts}
$\sum_{a\in A}N_a(x)=n$ for every $x\in A^n$. Consequently, two words agreeing in all counts except possibly for one distinguished letter agree in that count too, hence have the same type.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Memoryless class]
With $\Delta(A)=\{\theta\in\mathbb{R}^A:\theta_a\ge0,\ \sum_a\theta_a=1\}$, the memoryless class on $A^n$ is $\Iclass(A,n)=\{p_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Delta(A)}$, $p_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^n\theta_{x_j}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Likelihood factors through the type]\label{lem:factor}
$p_\theta(x)=\prod_{a\in A}\theta_a^{N_a(x)}$; in particular $N(x)=N(y)$ implies $p_\theta(x)=p_\theta(y)$ for every $\theta$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Type bound at the Rissanen dimension]\label{thm:typebound}
Let $|A|=m\ge1$. Then
\[
\Cs\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)\le(n+1)^{m-1},\qquad \price\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)\le(m-1)\log_2(n+1)\ \text{bits}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Fix a distinguished letter $a_0$ and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:stat} with the reduced statistic $T(x)=(N_a(x))_{a\ne a_0}\in\{0,\dots,n\}^{A\setminus\{a_0\}}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:counts} the reduced statistic determines the full type, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:factor} the likelihood then depends only on it. The target set has $(n+1)^{m-1}$ elements.
\end{proof}

The exponent is exactly the dimension $d=m-1$ of the parameter simplex---one less than the alphabet size, because of the constraint $\sum_a\theta_a=1$. This matches the dimension in Rissanen's asymptotic $\tfrac d2\log_2 n+O(1)$; only the constant factor $2$ is lost.

\subsection{Packing gives lower bounds}

\begin{theorem}[Packing bound]\label{thm:packing}
Let $f:I\to\Xset$ be injective with $I$ finite, and $\theta:I\to\Theta$ arbitrary. Then
\[
\sum_{i\in I}p_{\theta(i)}\bigl(f(i)\bigr)\le\Cs(\Sclass).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each summand is at most $\ml(f(i))$; injectivity makes $\{f(i)\}$ a set of distinct messages, so the sum of $\ml$ over that set is a sub-sum of the nonnegative full sum defining $\Cs$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity]\label{thm:mono}
If for every $\theta'$ and $x$ there is $\theta$ with $p'_{\theta'}(x)\le p_\theta(x)$, then $\Cs(\Sclass')\le\Cs(\Sclass)$. In particular a subclass is never more expensive than the class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Alphabet lower bound]\label{thm:alphlower}
For $n\ge1$, $\Cs(\Iclass(A,n))\ge m$, i.e.\ $\price\ge\log_2 m$ bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:packing} with $I=A$, $f(a)=a^n$ (injective for $n\ge1$) and $\theta(a)=\delta_a$ the point mass on $a$: each of the $m$ terms equals $1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension sandwich]\label{thm:sandwich}
For $|A|=m$ and $n\ge1$,
\[
\log_2 m\ \le\ \price\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)\ \le\ (m-1)\log_2(n+1).
\]
\end{theorem}

The lower bound is independent of $n$: however long the message, the universal decompressor must still pay for naming the letter a deterministic source repeats.

\subsection{The binary benchmark}

For $A=\{0,1\}$ the Shtarkov sum is
\[
\Cs\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},n)\bigr)=\sum_{j=0}^n\binom nj\Bigl(\frac jn\Bigr)^{j}\Bigl(\frac{n-j}{n}\Bigr)^{n-j},
\]
since the maximum-likelihood bias of a word with $j$ ones is $j/n$. Two estimates bracket it:
\[
\frac{\sqrt n}{4}\ \le\ \Cs\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},n)\bigr)\ \le\ n+1\qquad(n\ge2),
\]
the upper bound being Theorem~\ref{thm:typebound} with $m=2$, the lower bound a central-window estimate: the $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ indices $j$ within $O(\sqrt n)$ of $n/2$ each contribute a term bounded below by a constant. In bits, $\tfrac12\log_2 n-2\le\price\le\log_2(n+1)$: the Rissanen half-logarithm for one free parameter.

\section{Tensorization: the price is additive over independent blocks}

\begin{definition}[Tensor product and powers]
For classes $\Sclass$ on $\Xset$ (parameters $\Theta$) and $\Tclass$ on $\mathcal{Y}$ (parameters $\Psi$), the tensor product $\Sclass\otimes\Tclass$ is the class on $\Xset\times\mathcal{Y}$ with parameters $\Theta\times\Psi$ and $p_{(\theta,\psi)}(x,y)=p_\theta(x)p_\psi(y)$. The $k$-th power $\Sclass^{\otimes k}$ is the class on $\Xset^k$ with parameters $\Theta^k$ and $p_{\vec\theta}(\vec x)=\prod_{i=1}^k p_{\theta_i}(x_i)$: $k$ blocks, each with its own independently chosen parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Division trick]\label{lem:div}
Let $c\ge0$, $P\ge0$ and suppose $c\,p_\theta(x)\le P$ for every $\theta$. Then $c\,\ml(x)\le P$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If $c=0$ this is $0\le P$. If $c>0$, then $p_\theta(x)\le P/c$ for all $\theta$, so $\ml(x)\le P/c$; multiply back.
\end{proof}

This device replaces a compactness/attainment argument and is what allows arbitrary, infinite parameter spaces.

\begin{theorem}[Maximum likelihood factorizes]\label{thm:mlfact}
$\ml_{\Sclass\otimes\Tclass}(x,y)=\ml_{\Sclass}(x)\,\ml_{\Tclass}(y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\le$) For every $(\theta,\psi)$, $p_\theta(x)p_\psi(y)\le\ml(x)\ml(y)$; take the supremum. ($\ge$) Write $P=\ml_{\Sclass\otimes\Tclass}(x,y)$. For fixed $\theta$, Lemma~\ref{lem:div} with $c=p_\theta(x)$ over $\psi$ gives $p_\theta(x)\ml_{\Tclass}(y)\le P$; then Lemma~\ref{lem:div} with $c=\ml_{\Tclass}(y)$ over $\theta$ gives $\ml_{\Tclass}(y)\ml_{\Sclass}(x)\le P$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Multiplicativity of the Shtarkov sum]\label{thm:mult}
\[
\Cs(\Sclass\otimes\Tclass)=\Cs(\Sclass)\,\Cs(\Tclass),\qquad \Cs(\Sclass^{\otimes k})=\Cs(\Sclass)^k,
\]
equivalently $\price(\Sclass^{\otimes k})=k\,\price(\Sclass)$: the price of universality is \emph{additive} over independently parameterized blocks.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Sum Theorem~\ref{thm:mlfact} over $\Xset\times\mathcal{Y}$ and use the product-of-sums identity. For powers, one proves $\ml_{\Sclass^{\otimes k}}(\vec x)=\prod_i\ml(x_i)$ by induction over coordinates: for a set $s$ of already-maximized coordinates,
\[
\Bigl(\prod_{i\in s}\ml(x_i)\Bigr)\Bigl(\prod_{i\notin s}p_{\theta_i}(x_i)\Bigr)\ \le\ \ml_{\Sclass^{\otimes k}}(\vec x)
\]
for every $\vec\theta$, upgrading one coordinate at a time with Lemma~\ref{lem:div}; take $s$ to be all coordinates.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A multi-alphabet lower bound by tensorization}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding the binary power]\label{thm:embed}
Let $A=\{0,1\}^k$, so $|A|=2^k$. Then $\Cs\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},n)^{\otimes k}\bigr)\le\Cs\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A word $x\in A^n$ is the same data as a $k$-tuple of binary words of length $n$. Given Bernoulli parameters $\vec\theta$, the product parameter $\theta^\otimes(a)=\prod_i\theta_i(a_i)$ lies in $\Delta(A)$, and both likelihoods equal $\prod_j\prod_i\theta_i(x_{j,i})$ after commuting products. Hence each maximum likelihood of the power class is dominated by one of the memoryless class over $A$; sum along the transposition bijection.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multi-alphabet lower bound]\label{cor:multilower}
For $n\ge2$ and $|A|=2^k$,
\[
\Cs\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)\ \ge\ \Bigl(\frac{\sqrt n}{4}\Bigr)^{k},\qquad
\price\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)\ \ge\ k\Bigl(\tfrac12\log_2 n-2\Bigr).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Multi-alphabet sandwich]\label{thm:multisandwich}
For $|A|=2^k$ and $n\ge2$,
\[
k\Bigl(\tfrac12\log_2 n-2\Bigr)\ \le\ \price\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)\ \le\ (2^k-1)\log_2(n+1).
\]
\end{theorem}

Both sides are logarithmic in $n$; the alphabet-dependent constant is unbounded, at least linear in $k=\log_2|A|$ and at most the parameter dimension $|A|-1$.

\subsection{The sharing dichotomy}

\begin{theorem}[Independent versus shared parameters]\label{thm:dichotomy}
Fix $n\ge2$, $k\ge1$, and binary data of total length $kn$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Independent.) For $k$ blocks of length $n$, each with its own bias,
$\price\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},n)^{\otimes k}\bigr)=k\,\price\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},n)\bigr)\ge k\bigl(\tfrac12\log_2 n-2\bigr)$.
\item (Shared.) For one bias governing all $kn$ symbols,
$\price\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},kn)\bigr)\le\log_2(kn+1)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Explicit linear gap]\label{thm:gap}
With blocks of length $32$, for every $k\ge5000$,
\[
\price\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},32)^{\otimes k}\bigr)-\price\bigl(\Iclass(\{0,1\},32k)\bigr)\ \ge\ \frac k4\ \text{bits}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:dichotomy}(1) with $\log_2 32=5$, the independent price is at least $k(\tfrac52-2)=k/2$. For the shared price, $\log_2(32k+1)\le2.9\sqrt{32k+1}\le2.9\sqrt{33k}$, using $\log_2 t\le2.9\sqrt t$ for $t\ge1$ (from $\log\sqrt t\le\sqrt t-1$ and $\log2>0.693$). For $k\ge5000$, $\sqrt{33k}\ge406$ and hence $2.9\sqrt{33k}\le k/4$. Subtract.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Memorylessness is not what makes universality cheap; \emph{parameter sharing} is. Two classes with the same alphabet, total length and i.i.d.\ structure within blocks differ by an unbounded number of bits according to whether the parameter is shared or replicated per block. Those $\Theta(k)$ bits are exactly the bits a decompressor that already knows the $k$ parameters gets for free.
\end{remark}

\section{Model selection: serving many specialized classes at once}

\begin{definition}[Union of classes]
For finitely many classes $\Sclass_i$ on a common message set, the union $\bigsqcup_i\Sclass_i$ has parameter set $\coprod_i\Theta_i$ and $p_{(i,\theta)}=p^{(i)}_\theta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Subadditivity]\label{thm:subadd}
$\Cs\bigl(\bigsqcup_i\Sclass_i\bigr)\le\sum_i\Cs(\Sclass_i)$, and $\Cs(\Sclass_i)\le\Cs\bigl(\bigsqcup_j\Sclass_j\bigr)$ for every $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Model-selection overhead]\label{thm:modelsel}
If $\Cs(\Sclass_i)\le B$ for each of $M$ classes, then
$\price\bigl(\bigsqcup_i\Sclass_i\bigr)\le\log_2 M+\log_2 B$. For two classes, $\price(\Sclass\sqcup\Tclass)\le1+\max\{\price(\Sclass),\price(\Tclass)\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The overhead is attained]\label{thm:attained}
If the models are mutually singular---pairwise disjoint sets $U_i$ with $p^{(i)}_\theta(x)=0$ for $x\notin U_i$---then $\Cs\bigl(\bigsqcup_i\Sclass_i\bigr)=\sum_i\Cs(\Sclass_i)$; if all $\Cs(\Sclass_i)$ equal $C$, then $\price\bigl(\bigsqcup_i\Sclass_i\bigr)=\log_2 M+\log_2 C$ exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Off $\bigcup_i U_i$ all maximum likelihoods vanish; on $U_i$, sources from other models contribute $0$, so the union's maximum likelihood coincides with $\ml_i$. Split the sum over the disjoint union.
\end{proof}

Thus $\log_2 M$ bits---the cost of \emph{naming the model}---is exactly the price of keeping $M$ specialized models under one shared decompressor: doubling the library costs one bit. This is the information-theoretic content of two-part codes and minimum-description-length model selection.

\begin{theorem}[Twice-universal coding]\label{thm:twice}
Let $|A|=m$. The first-order Markov class on messages of length $n+1$ satisfies $\Cs\le m(n+1)^{m^2}$ by the method of types applied to transition counts. Consequently a single decompressor serving both the memoryless and the first-order Markov class on messages of length $n+1$ pays at most
\[
1+\log_2 m+m^2\log_2(n+2)\ \text{bits},
\]
one bit more than the Markov class alone.
\end{theorem}

\section{Finite-state sources and the vanishing per-symbol price}

\begin{definition}[Finite-state source]
Fix a finite alphabet $A$, a finite state set $S$, a deterministic transition $\delta:S\times A\to S$ and an initial state $s_0$. A parameter is an emission law $g:S\to\Delta(A)$. The likelihood on $A^n$ is defined recursively by $p^{(0)}_g(\varepsilon\mid s)=1$ and $p^{(n+1)}_g(x\mid s)=g_s(x_1)\,p^{(n)}_g(x_2\cdots x_{n+1}\mid\delta(s,x_1))$; the class is $\Fclass(\delta,s_0,n)$. Order-$r$ Markov sources are the case $S=A^r$ with the shift transition.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Normalization]\label{lem:fsmnorm}
$\sum_{x\in A^n}p^{(n)}_g(x\mid s)=1$ for every $n$ and $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction on $n$: split over the first letter $a$; the inner sum is $g_s(a)$ times the total mass at $\delta(s,a)$, which is $1$; then $\sum_a g_s(a)=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Trajectory product form]\label{lem:fsmprod}
With $s_1=s_0$ and $s_{j+1}=\delta(s_j,x_j)$, one has $p^{(n)}_g(x\mid s_0)=\prod_{j=1}^n g_{s_j}(x_j)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-state type bound]\label{thm:fsmbound}
\[
\Cs\bigl(\Fclass(\delta,s_0,n)\bigr)\le(n+1)^{|S|\,|A|},\qquad \price\le|S|\,|A|\log_2(n+1)\ \text{bits}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:fsmprod} the likelihood is $\prod_{(s,a)}g_s(a)^{N_{s,a}(x)}$ where $N_{s,a}$ counts positions with state $s$ and letter $a$. Since $\delta$ and $s_0$ are fixed and deterministic, the trajectory---hence $N$---is a function of $x$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:stat} applies with $|S||A|$ counts each ranging over $n+1$ values.
\end{proof}

If $|S|=1$ the trajectory is constant, the class \emph{is} the memoryless class, and the bound degenerates to $(n+1)^{|A|}$, consistent with Section~2.

\begin{theorem}[The per-symbol price vanishes]\label{thm:rate}
For every finite alphabet $A$ and every finite automaton $(S,\delta,s_0)$,
\[
0\ \le\ \frac{\price\bigl(\Fclass(\delta,s_0,n)\bigr)}{n}\ \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\ 0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Non-negativity is Proposition~\ref{prop:nonneg}. For the limit, squeeze between $0$ and $c\log_2(n+1)/n$ with $c=|S||A|$, using Theorem~\ref{thm:fsmbound}.
\end{proof}

The automaton may be arbitrarily large; only the constant changes. Specializing the decompressor to a \emph{parametric} class therefore cannot move more than $o(n)$ bits out of a length-$n$ message.

\section{Symmetry, not parametricity}

\begin{definition}[Exchangeable class]
A class on $A^n$ is \emph{exchangeable} if $p_\theta(x_{\sigma(1)},\dots,x_{\sigma(n)})=p_\theta(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ for every parameter $\theta$, message $x$ and permutation $\sigma$ of positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equal types means permutation]\label{thm:perm}
If $x,y\in A^n$ satisfy $N(x)=N(y)$, there is a permutation $\sigma$ of positions with $y_{\sigma(j)}=x_j$ for all $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For each letter $b$, the fibers $\{j:x_j=b\}$ and $\{j:y_j=b\}$ have equal cardinality, so admit a bijection $e_b$. Composing the decomposition $\{1,\dots,n\}\simeq\coprod_b\{j:x_j=b\}$, the fiberwise bijections $\coprod_b e_b$, and the reassembly $\coprod_b\{j:y_j=b\}\simeq\{1,\dots,n\}$ yields the desired permutation.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Type-invariant classes are cheap]\label{thm:typeinv}
If $N(x)=N(y)\Rightarrow p_\theta(x)=p_\theta(y)$ for all $\theta$, then $\Cs(\Sclass)\le(n+1)^{|A|-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exchangeable classes are cheap]\label{thm:exch}
Every exchangeable class on $A^n$---of arbitrary cardinality, parametric or not---satisfies
\[
\Cs(\Sclass)\le(n+1)^{|A|-1},\qquad \price(\Sclass)\le(|A|-1)\log_2(n+1)\ \text{bits},
\]
and over a binary alphabet $\price(\Sclass)\le\log_2(n+1)$ bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Combine Theorems~\ref{thm:perm} and~\ref{thm:typeinv}: equal types make $x$ a permutation of $y$, and invariance gives $p_\theta(x)=p_\theta(y)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The class of \emph{all} exchangeable sources on $\{0,1\}^n$ is uncountable and non-parametric. By de Finetti's theorem its infinite-sequence members are mixtures of i.i.d.\ Bernoulli laws, but Theorem~\ref{thm:exch} needs no such representation and covers finite-$n$ exchangeable laws (P\'olya urns, sampling without replacement, arbitrary symmetric measures) that are not i.i.d.\ mixtures. All are served by one code at $\log_2(n+1)$ bits of redundancy. Consequently, any class whose price is superlogarithmic must break permutation symmetry---as the independent-block classes of Section~3 do.
\end{remark}

\section{Algorithms}

\subsection{Exact Shtarkov sum for the memoryless class}

The maximum-likelihood parameter of a word of type $N$ is $\widehat\theta_a=N_a/n$, and each type contains $\binom{n}{N}=n!/\prod_a N_a!$ words, so
\[
\Cs\bigl(\Iclass(A,n)\bigr)=\sum_{\substack{N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^A\\ \sum_a N_a=n}}\binom nN\prod_{a\in A}\Bigl(\frac{N_a}{n}\Bigr)^{N_a},
\]
with $0^0=1$: a sum over $\binom{n+m-1}{m-1}$ compositions, computable in log-space arithmetic. Asymptotically,
\[
\log \Cs=\frac{m-1}{2}\log\frac{n}{2\pi}+\log\frac{\pi^{m/2}}{\Gamma(m/2)}+o(1),
\]
which for $m=2$ reads $\Cs\sim\sqrt{\pi n/2}$.

\subsection{Normalized maximum likelihood encoding}

The optimal universal code assigns $x$ length $-\log_2\ml(x)+\log_2\Cs$. Since $\ml$ depends only on the type, it can be implemented enumeratively: encode the type among the $\binom{n+m-1}{m-1}$ types, then the index of $x$ within its type class using $\log_2\binom nN$ bits.

\subsection{Certifying a lower bound by packing}

Given distinct messages $x_i$ and sources $\theta_i$, the number $\sum_i p_{\theta_i}(x_i)$ certifies $\price\ge\log_2\sum_i p_{\theta_i}(x_i)$. Choosing the $\theta_i$ on a $\Theta(1/\sqrt n)$-separated grid in the simplex, with $x_i$ a typical message of $\theta_i$, is the route to the conjectured $\tfrac d2\log_2 n$.

\section{Numerical illustrations}

Exact Shtarkov sums for the binary memoryless class:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{rrrrrr}
\toprule
$n$ & $\Cs$ & $\price=\log_2\Cs$ & $\tfrac12\log_2 n-2$ & $\log_2(n+1)$ & $\log_2\sqrt{\pi n/2}$\\
\midrule
8    & 4.245  & 2.086 & $-0.500$ & 3.170  & 1.826\\
32   & 7.774  & 2.959 & 0.500    & 5.044  & 2.826\\
128  & 14.855 & 3.893 & 1.500    & 7.011  & 3.826\\
1024 & 40.776 & 5.350 & 3.000    & 10.001 & 5.326\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The exact price tracks $\tfrac12\log_2 n+0.326$ (discrepancy $0.26$ at $n=8$, $0.024$ at $n=1024$), sitting strictly between the proved bounds and confirming that the type bound overshoots the leading coefficient by about a factor of $2$.

For the sharing dichotomy with block length $32$, the independent-block price is exactly $k\cdot2.959$ bits while the shared-parameter price on $32k$ symbols is about $\tfrac12\log_2(32k)+0.326$. At $k=5000$ these are $14\,793$ bits versus $8.97$ bits: the specialized decompressor absorbs more than $14\,780$ bits that the universal one must charge to the message.

\section{Discussion: the verdict on specialization}

\textbf{Against specialization.} For any parametric class with a shared parameter---memoryless, Markov of any order, finite-state with any automaton---the price of universality is $O(\log n)$ bits on a message of $n$ symbols, and per symbol it tends to zero (Theorem~\ref{thm:rate}). A universal decompressor asymptotically matches a specialized one on a rate basis. Even non-parametric classes escape only by breaking permutation symmetry (Theorem~\ref{thm:exch}).

\textbf{For specialization.} The price is exactly additive over independently parameterized blocks (Theorem~\ref{thm:mult}). Whenever data is a concatenation of many short, heterogeneously parameterized records---per-file models, per-user profiles, per-sensor calibrations---the universal price grows linearly in the number of records (Theorem~\ref{thm:gap}), and a decompressor carrying those parameters absorbs all of it.

\textbf{A cheap hedge.} Maintaining $M$ specialized models in one decompressor costs $\log_2 M$ bits, once (Theorem~\ref{thm:modelsel}), and no less when the models are mutually singular (Theorem~\ref{thm:attained}). Build a library of specialized models and pay a model index; do not attempt a single monolithic model of everything.

\textbf{Relation to the classical literature.} Our upper bounds carry the exact Rissanen parameter dimension $d$ in the exponent, and the binary lower bound has the correct $\tfrac d2\log_2 n$ leading behavior for $d=1$; the multi-alphabet lower bound has leading coefficient $\tfrac12\log_2 m$. The conjectured truth $\tfrac d2\log_2 n+O(1)$ is therefore bracketed everywhere, the remaining gap being a factor $2$ in the leading coefficient for large alphabets.

\section{Open problems and future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[The factor-2 conjecture]
For fixed $|A|=m$ there are constants $0<c_1\le c_2$ with $c_1 n^{(m-1)/2}\le\Cs(\Iclass(A,n))\le c_2 n^{(m-1)/2}$ for all $n\ge1$; equivalently $\log_2\Cs=\tfrac{m-1}{2}\log_2 n+O(1)$, whereas the proved bounds are $\tfrac{\log_2 m}{2}\log_2 n-2\log_2 m$ from below and $(m-1)\log_2(n+1)$ from above.
\end{conjecture}

The key insight is that $\Cs$ is a sum over types, and Stirling turns each type's contribution into a Gaussian weight: $\Cs$ is a Riemann sum for $\int\sqrt{\det I(\theta)}\,d\theta$ over the simplex, so the exponent is \emph{half} the dimension, the missing factor $\tfrac12$ being exactly the Jacobian of the maximum-likelihood map. The one-dimensional case is settled; the general case needs a multivariate local central limit theorem for the multinomial, or a purely combinatorial packing over a $\sqrt n$-grid of types.

\begin{conjecture}[The price is a dimension-additive invariant]
Define $\dim(\Sclass)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\log_2\Cs(\Sclass_n)/\log_2 n$. Then $\dim$ is additive over tensor products and satisfies $\dim(\text{i.i.d.\ over }A)=\tfrac{|A|-1}{2}$, $\dim(\text{order-1 Markov over }A)=\tfrac{|A|(|A|-1)}{2}$, and $\dim(\text{finite-state with states }S)=\tfrac{|S|(|A|-1)}{2}$.
\end{conjecture}

Exact multiplicativity of $\Cs$ makes the price a dimension-like invariant of a source class---an ``entropy of the model space'' that adds under independent composition, exactly like Hausdorff dimension under products. Multiplicativity holds for arbitrary parameter spaces via the division trick, so the invariant is well defined; what remains is to compute it for the three families.

\begin{conjecture}[Sharing is the only cheap regime]
For every $\alpha\in(0,1]$ there is a class of sources on $A^n$ whose price is $\Theta(n^\alpha)$; and every class whose price is $\omega(\log n)$ fails to be exchangeable in a quantitative sense, the price being controlled by the number of orbits of the symmetry group of the class acting on the message space---interpolating between the exchangeable case ($(n+1)^{|A|-1}$ orbits, logarithmic price) and the fully independent case ($|A|^n$ orbits, linear price).
\end{conjecture}

Further directions: (a) extend model selection to countably infinite libraries with a Kraft-summable prior, recovering the classical two-part minimum-description-length code; (b) quantify the price for context-tree sources of unbounded depth, where the parameter count itself grows with $n$; (c) study the sequential (online) version, where the code must be a predictor---the minimax regret is the same $\log_2\Cs$, but the horizon-free version is strictly more expensive; (d) make the packing certificate algorithmic, computing near-optimal $\sqrt n$-grids to certify lower bounds within $O(1)$ of the truth for moderate $m$ and $n$.

and the minimax pointwise redundancy -- the *price of universality*, i.e. the

code tailored to the true source -- equals exactly log2(C_S), attained by the
normalized maximum likelihood (NML) code q*(x) = sup_theta p_theta(x) / C_S.

What this script demonstrates:

 3. Exact multiplicativity of the Shtarkov sum under independent composition,
    C_S(S x T) = C_S(S) * C_S(T), verified by brute force on small classes.
 4. The sharing dichotomy: k independently parameterised blocks cost a price
    LINEAR in k, while one shared parameter over the same total length costs
    only a LOGARITHMIC price.
 5. The model-selection overhead: a union of M classes costs at most
    log2 M + max price, with equality for mutually singular models.
 6. Finite-state sources: the per-symbol price |S||A| log2(n+1) / n -> 0.
 7. Exchangeability: an arbitrary, non-parametric permutation-invariant class
    obeys the same (n+1)^(m-1) bound as the memoryless family.

Only the Python standard library is used.

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Exact Shtarkov sums for the memoryless class, by the method of types
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def compositions(n: int, m: int) -> Iterable[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Enumerate all m-tuples of nonnegative integers summing to n."""
    if m == 1:
        yield (n,)
        return
    for first in range(n + 1):
        for rest in compositions(n - first, m - 1):
            yield (first,) + rest


def multinomial(counts: Sequence[int]) -> int:
    """Number of words of length sum(counts) with the given letter counts."""
    total = sum(counts)
    value = math.factorial(total)
    for c in counts:
        value //= math.factorial(c)
    return value


def type_max_likelihood(counts: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """max_theta prod_a theta_a^{N_a} = prod_a (N_a/n)^{N_a}, with 0^0 = 1.

    The maximum-likelihood parameter of a word of type N is the empirical
    distribution theta_a = N_a / n.
    """
    n = sum(counts)
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    value = 1.0
    for c in counts:
        if c > 0:
            value *= (c / n) ** c
    return value


def shtarkov_iid(n: int, m: int) -> float:
    """Exact Shtarkov sum of the memoryless class on A^n with |A| = m.

    C_S = sum over types N of  multinomial(N) * prod_a (N_a/n)^{N_a}.
    Complexity: O(binom(n+m-1, m-1)) terms.
    """
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    return sum(
        multinomial(counts) * type_max_likelihood(counts)
        for counts in compositions(n, m)
    )


def shtarkov_iid_log2(n: int, m: int) -> float:
    """log2 of the exact Shtarkov sum, computed stably in log space."""
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0
    terms: List[float] = []
    for counts in compositions(n, m):
        log_term = math.lgamma(n + 1)
        for c in counts:
            log_term -= math.lgamma(c + 1)
            if c > 0:
                log_term += c * math.log(c / n)
        terms.append(log_term)
    peak = max(terms)
    total = sum(math.exp(t - peak) for t in terms)
    return (peak + math.log(total)) / math.log(2.0)


def rissanen_asymptotic_log2(n: int, m: int) -> float:
    """The Shtarkov--Rissanen asymptotic for log2 C_S of the i.i.d. class:

        log C_S = ((m-1)/2) log(n / (2 pi)) + log( pi^{m/2} / Gamma(m/2) ) + o(1).

    For m = 2 this is log2 sqrt(pi n / 2).
    """
    ln = (m - 1) / 2.0 * math.log(n / (2.0 * math.pi)) + (
        (m / 2.0) * math.log(math.pi) - math.lgamma(m / 2.0)
    )
    return ln / math.log(2.0)


def demo_iid_sandwich() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("1.  Memoryless class: exact price versus the proved sandwich")
    print("=" * 78)
    print("    log2 m  <=  log2 C_S  <=  (m-1) log2(n+1)")
    print()
    for m in (2, 3, 4):
        print(f"  alphabet size m = {m}")
        header = f"    {'n':>6} {'C_S':>14} {'log2 C_S':>10} {'lower':>8} {'upper':>8} {'asympt':>9}"
        print(header)

            c = shtarkov_iid(n, m)
            price = math.log2(c)
            lower = math.log2(m)
            upper = (m - 1) * math.log2(n + 1)

            assert price <= upper + 1e-9, "type upper bound violated"
            print(f"    {n:>6} {c:>14.4f} {price:>10.4f} {lower:>8.4f} {upper:>8.4f} {asym:>9.4f}")
        print()

# 3.  Multiplicativity of the Shtarkov sum, verified by brute force
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


Distribution = Tuple[float, ...]


def shtarkov_of_finite_class(sources: Sequence[Distribution]) -> float:
    """C_S of a class given as an explicit finite list of distributions."""
    n_messages = len(sources[0])
    return sum(max(p[x] for p in sources) for x in range(n_messages))


def tensor_class(
    left: Sequence[Distribution], right: Sequence[Distribution]
) -> List[Distribution]:
    """All product sources p_theta (x) p_psi on the product message set."""
    out: List[Distribution] = []
    for p in left:
        for q in right:
            out.append(tuple(pi * qi for pi in p for qi in q))
    return out


def random_class(n_sources: int, n_messages: int, rng: random.Random) -> List[Distribution]:
    """A random source class: n_sources distributions on n_messages messages."""
    cls: List[Distribution] = []
    for _ in range(n_sources):
        weights = [rng.random() + 1e-3 for _ in range(n_messages)]
        total = sum(weights)
        cls.append(tuple(w / total for w in weights))
    return cls


def demo_multiplicativity() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3.  Exact multiplicativity:  C_S(S (x) T) = C_S(S) * C_S(T)")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(20260818)
    print(f"    {'trial':>6} {'C_S(S)':>10} {'C_S(T)':>10} {'product':>12} {'C_S(S(x)T)':>12} {'error':>10}")
    for trial in range(1, 6):
        s = random_class(rng.randint(2, 5), rng.randint(2, 5), rng)
        t = random_class(rng.randint(2, 5), rng.randint(2, 5), rng)
        cs, ct = shtarkov_of_finite_class(s), shtarkov_of_finite_class(t)
        cst = shtarkov_of_finite_class(tensor_class(s, t))
        err = abs(cst - cs * ct)
        assert err < 1e-12, "multiplicativity failed"
        print(f"    {trial:>6} {cs:>10.6f} {ct:>10.6f} {cs * ct:>12.6f} {cst:>12.6f} {err:>10.2e}")
    print()
    print("    Consequence: the price of universality is ADDITIVE over")
    print("    independently parameterised blocks:  R(S^k) = k * R(S).")
    print()

def union_class(classes: Sequence[Sequence[Distribution]]) -> List[Distribution]:
    """The union of several classes on a common message set."""
    return [p for cls in classes for p in cls]

def fsm_price_bound_bits(n_states: int, alphabet_size: int, n: int) -> float:
    """The proved bound |S| * |A| * log2(n+1) on the price of a finite-state class."""
    return n_states * alphabet_size * math.log2(n + 1)


def fsm_likelihood(
    transition: Callable[[int, int], int],
    emission: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
    initial_state: int,
    word: Sequence[int],
) -> float:
    """Likelihood of a word under a finite-state source: the product of the
    emission probabilities along the deterministic state trajectory."""
    state = initial_state
    value = 1.0
    for letter in word:
        value *= emission[state][letter]
        state = transition(state, letter)
    return value


def demo_finite_state() -> None:

    lik = fsm_likelihood(transition, emission, 0, word)
    print(f"    two-state automaton (state = previous letter), emission {emission}")
    print(f"    likelihood of {word} = {lik:.8f}")
    total = sum(

        for w in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=len(word))
    )
    print(f"    total mass over all {2 ** len(word)} words of that length = {total:.12f}")
    assert abs(total - 1.0) < 1e-12
    print()
    print("    proved bound   price <= |S| * |A| * log2(n+1)   and price/n -> 0:")
    print(f"    {'n':>9} {'|S|=2,|A|=2':>13} {'per symbol':>12} {'|S|=64,|A|=256':>16} {'per symbol':>12}")

    print()
    print("    A large automaton only changes the constant, never the rate.")

# 7.  Exchangeability: symmetry, not parametricity, is what makes coding cheap
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def word_type(word: Sequence[int], alphabet_size: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    counts = [0] * alphabet_size
    for letter in word:
        counts[letter] += 1
    return tuple(counts)


def random_exchangeable_source(
    n: int, alphabet_size: int, rng: random.Random
) -> Dict[Tuple[int, ...], float]:
    """A random exchangeable law on A^n: an arbitrary probability vector over
    TYPES, spread uniformly inside each type class.  No i.i.d. structure, no
    parameters -- just permutation invariance."""
    types = list(compositions(n, alphabet_size))
    weights = [rng.random() for _ in types]
    total = sum(weights)
    return {t: w / total / multinomial(t) for t, w in zip(types, weights)}


def demo_exchangeable() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("7.  Exchangeable classes: cheap however wild")
    print("=" * 78)
    print("    Theorem:  ANY permutation-invariant class on A^n has")
    print("              C_S <= (n+1)^(|A|-1),  price <= (|A|-1) log2(n+1).")
    print()
    rng = random.Random(31415)
    for n, m, n_sources in ((6, 2, 40), (8, 2, 60), (5, 3, 40)):
        sources = [random_exchangeable_source(n, m, rng) for _ in range(n_sources)]
        words = list(itertools.product(range(m), repeat=n))
        # sanity: each source is a probability distribution and is exchangeable
        for src in sources[:3]:
            mass = sum(src[word_type(w, m)] for w in words)
            assert abs(mass - 1.0) < 1e-9
        c_s = sum(max(src[word_type(w, m)] for src in sources) for w in words)
        price = math.log2(c_s)
        bound = (m - 1) * math.log2(n + 1)
        assert price <= bound + 1e-9
        print(
            f"    n={n:>2}, |A|={m}, {n_sources} random exchangeable sources:"
            f"  price = {price:.4f} bits  <=  bound {bound:.4f} bits"
        )
    print()
    print("    Even the class of ALL exchangeable laws is bounded the same way:")
    for n in (10, 100, 1000):
        print(f"        binary, n = {n:>4}:  price <= log2(n+1) = {math.log2(n + 1):.4f} bits")
    print()

def nml_code_lengths(n: int, m: int) -> Dict[Tuple[int, ...], float]:
    """Code length (in bits) that the optimal universal code assigns to each
    type class of A^n for the memoryless class:
        -log2 maxlik(N) + log2 C_S   for one representative word of type N.
    """
    c_s = shtarkov_iid(n, m)
    lengths: Dict[Tuple[int, ...], float] = {}
    for counts in compositions(n, m):
        lengths[counts] = -math.log2(type_max_likelihood(counts)) + math.log2(c_s)
    return lengths

def binary_price_bits(n: int) -> float:
    """Exact price log2 C_S of the binary memoryless class on {0,1}^n, by types."""
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0
    lf = math.lgamma(n + 1)
    terms: List[float] = []
    for j in range(n + 1):
        t = lf - math.lgamma(j + 1) - math.lgamma(n - j + 1)
        if j > 0:
            t += j * math.log(j / n)
        if n - j > 0:
            t += (n - j) * math.log((n - j) / n)
        terms.append(t)
    peak = max(terms)
    return (peak + math.log(sum(math.exp(x - peak) for x in terms))) / math.log(2.0)

def worst_case_redundancy(cls: Sequence[Distribution], q: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """max over messages and sources of log2( p_theta(x) / q(x) )."""
    ml = max_likelihood(cls)
    worst = -math.inf
    for x, m in enumerate(ml):
        if q[x] <= 0.0:
            return math.inf
        worst = max(worst, math.log2(m / q[x]))
    return worst


def random_code(n_messages: int, rng: random.Random) -> List[float]:
    w = [rng.random() + 1e-6 for _ in range(n_messages)]
    total = sum(w)
    return [x / total for x in w]


def perturb(q: Sequence[float], scale: float, rng: random.Random) -> List[float]:
    w = [max(1e-9, v * math.exp(rng.gauss(0.0, scale))) for v in q]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Exact Shtarkov sums for the memoryless class, by the method of types
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def compositions(n: int, m: int) -> Iterable[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Enumerate all m-tuples of nonnegative integers summing to n."""
    if m == 1:
        yield (n,)
        return
    for first in range(n + 1):
        for rest in compositions(n - first, m - 1):
            yield (first,) + rest


def multinomial(counts: Sequence[int]) -> int:
    """Number of words of length sum(counts) with the given letter counts."""
    total = sum(counts)
    value = math.factorial(total)
    for c in counts:
        value //= math.factorial(c)
    return value


def type_max_likelihood(counts: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """max_theta prod_a theta_a^{N_a} = prod_a (N_a/n)^{N_a}, with 0^0 = 1.

    The maximum-likelihood parameter of a word of type N is the empirical
    distribution theta_a = N_a / n.
    """
    n = sum(counts)
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    value = 1.0
    for c in counts:
        if c > 0:
            value *= (c / n) ** c
    return value


def shtarkov_iid(n: int, m: int) -> float:
    """Exact Shtarkov sum of the memoryless class on A^n with |A| = m.

    C_S = sum over types N of  multinomial(N) * prod_a (N_a/n)^{N_a}.
    Complexity: O(binom(n+m-1, m-1)) terms.
    """
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    return sum(
        multinomial(counts) * type_max_likelihood(counts)
        for counts in compositions(n, m)
    )


def shtarkov_iid_log2(n: int, m: int) -> float:
    """log2 of the exact Shtarkov sum, computed stably in log space."""
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0
    terms: List[float] = []
    for counts in compositions(n, m):
        log_term = math.lgamma(n + 1)
        for c in counts:
            log_term -= math.lgamma(c + 1)
            if c > 0:
                log_term += c * math.log(c / n)
        terms.append(log_term)
    peak = max(terms)
    total = sum(math.exp(t - peak) for t in terms)
    return (peak + math.log(total)) / math.log(2.0)


def rissanen_asymptotic_log2(n: int, m: int) -> float:
    """The Shtarkov--Rissanen asymptotic for log2 C_S of the i.i.d. class:

        log C_S = ((m-1)/2) log(n / (2 pi)) + log( pi^{m/2} / Gamma(m/2) ) + o(1).

    For m = 2 this is log2 sqrt(pi n / 2).
    """
    ln = (m - 1) / 2.0 * math.log(n / (2.0 * math.pi)) + (
        (m / 2.0) * math.log(math.pi) - math.lgamma(m / 2.0)
    )
    return ln / math.log(2.0)

# 3.  Multiplicativity of the Shtarkov sum, verified by brute force
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


Distribution = Tuple[float, ...]


def shtarkov_of_finite_class(sources: Sequence[Distribution]) -> float:
    """C_S of a class given as an explicit finite list of distributions."""
    n_messages = len(sources[0])
    return sum(max(p[x] for p in sources) for x in range(n_messages))


def tensor_class(
    left: Sequence[Distribution], right: Sequence[Distribution]
) -> List[Distribution]:
    """All product sources p_theta (x) p_psi on the product message set."""
    out: List[Distribution] = []
    for p in left:
        for q in right:
            out.append(tuple(pi * qi for pi in p for qi in q))
    return out


def random_class(n_sources: int, n_messages: int, rng: random.Random) -> List[Distribution]:
    """A random source class: n_sources distributions on n_messages messages."""
    cls: List[Distribution] = []
    for _ in range(n_sources):
        weights = [rng.random() + 1e-3 for _ in range(n_messages)]
        total = sum(weights)
        cls.append(tuple(w / total for w in weights))
    return cls


def demo_multiplicativity() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3.  Exact multiplicativity:  C_S(S (x) T) = C_S(S) * C_S(T)")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(20260818)
    print(f"    {'trial':>6} {'C_S(S)':>10} {'C_S(T)':>10} {'product':>12} {'C_S(S(x)T)':>12} {'error':>10}")
    for trial in range(1, 6):
        s = random_class(rng.randint(2, 5), rng.randint(2, 5), rng)
        t = random_class(rng.randint(2, 5), rng.randint(2, 5), rng)
        cs, ct = shtarkov_of_finite_class(s), shtarkov_of_finite_class(t)
        cst = shtarkov_of_finite_class(tensor_class(s, t))
        err = abs(cst - cs * ct)
        assert err < 1e-12, "multiplicativity failed"
        print(f"    {trial:>6} {cs:>10.6f} {ct:>10.6f} {cs * ct:>12.6f} {cst:>12.6f} {err:>10.2e}")
    print()
    print("    Consequence: the price of universality is ADDITIVE over")
    print("    independently parameterised blocks:  R(S^k) = k * R(S).")
    print()

def demo_sharing_dichotomy(block_length: int = 32) -> None:

def union_class(classes: Sequence[Sequence[Distribution]]) -> List[Distribution]:
    """The union of several classes on a common message set."""
    return [p for cls in classes for p in cls]


def demo_model_selection() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("5.  Model selection: log2 M bits to name the model, and no more")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(11235)

    # (a) generic overlapping models: strict subadditivity.
    n_messages = 8
    models = [random_class(3, n_messages, rng) for _ in range(4)]
    prices = [math.log2(shtarkov_of_finite_class(c)) for c in models]
    union_price = math.log2(shtarkov_of_finite_class(union_class(models)))
    bound = math.log2(len(models)) + max(prices)
    print("    (a) four generic overlapping models on 8 messages")
    print(f"        individual prices : {[f'{p:.4f}' for p in prices]}")
    print(f"        union price       : {union_price:.4f} bits")
    print(f"        bound log2 M + max: {bound:.4f} bits")
    print(f"        every member <= union: {all(p <= union_price + 1e-12 for p in prices)}")
    assert union_price <= bound + 1e-12

    # (b) mutually singular models: the log2 M overhead is exactly attained.
    print()
    print("    (b) four MUTUALLY SINGULAR models (disjoint supports)")
    block = 4
    singular: List[List[Distribution]] = []
    for i in range(4):
        cls: List[Distribution] = []
        for p in random_class(3, block, rng):

            cls.append(tuple(full))
        singular.append(cls)
    sing_prices = [math.log2(shtarkov_of_finite_class(c)) for c in singular]
    sing_union = math.log2(shtarkov_of_finite_class(union_class(singular)))
    exact = math.log2(sum(shtarkov_of_finite_class(c) for c in singular))
    print(f"        individual prices : {[f'{p:.4f}' for p in sing_prices]}")
    print(f"        union price       : {sing_union:.4f} bits")
    print(f"        sum of Shtarkov sums (exact identity): {exact:.4f} bits")
    print(f"        overhead over the max member: {sing_union - max(sing_prices):.4f} bits"
          f"   (log2 4 = {math.log2(4):.4f} when the members are equal)")
    assert abs(sing_union - exact) < 1e-12
    print()

# 6.  Finite-state sources: the per-symbol price vanishes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def fsm_price_bound_bits(n_states: int, alphabet_size: int, n: int) -> float:
    """The proved bound |S| * |A| * log2(n+1) on the price of a finite-state class."""
    return n_states * alphabet_size * math.log2(n + 1)


def fsm_likelihood(
    transition: Callable[[int, int], int],
    emission: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
    initial_state: int,
    word: Sequence[int],
) -> float:
    """Likelihood of a word under a finite-state source: the product of the
    emission probabilities along the deterministic state trajectory."""
    state = initial_state
    value = 1.0
    for letter in word:
        value *= emission[state][letter]
        state = transition(state, letter)
    return value


def demo_finite_state() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6.  Finite-state sources: per-symbol price -> 0")
    print("=" * 78)

    # A concrete two-state automaton over a binary alphabet: state = last letter.
    transition = lambda _state, letter: letter
    emission = [[0.9, 0.1], [0.3, 0.7]]
    word = [0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1]
    lik = fsm_likelihood(transition, emission, 0, word)
    print(f"    two-state automaton (state = previous letter), emission {emission}")
    print(f"    likelihood of {word} = {lik:.8f}")
    total = sum(
        fsm_likelihood(transition, emission, 0, w)
        for w in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=len(word))
    )
    print(f"    total mass over all {2 ** len(word)} words of that length = {total:.12f}")
    assert abs(total - 1.0) < 1e-12
    print()
    print("    proved bound   price <= |S| * |A| * log2(n+1)   and price/n -> 0:")
    print(f"    {'n':>9} {'|S|=2,|A|=2':>13} {'per symbol':>12} {'|S|=64,|A|=256':>16} {'per symbol':>12}")
    for n in (10, 100, 10 ** 3, 10 ** 5, 10 ** 7, 10 ** 9):
        small = fsm_price_bound_bits(2, 2, n)
        big = fsm_price_bound_bits(64, 256, n)
        print(f"    {n:>9} {small:>13.2f} {small / n:>12.3e} {big:>16.2f} {big / n:>12.3e}")
    print()
    print("    A large automaton only changes the constant, never the rate.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.  Exchangeability: symmetry, not parametricity, is what makes coding cheap
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def word_type(word: Sequence[int], alphabet_size: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    counts = [0] * alphabet_size
    for letter in word:
        counts[letter] += 1
    return tuple(counts)


def random_exchangeable_source(
    n: int, alphabet_size: int, rng: random.Random
) -> Dict[Tuple[int, ...], float]:
    """A random exchangeable law on A^n: an arbitrary probability vector over
    TYPES, spread uniformly inside each type class.  No i.i.d. structure, no
    parameters -- just permutation invariance."""
    types = list(compositions(n, alphabet_size))
    weights = [rng.random() for _ in types]
    total = sum(weights)
    return {t: w / total / multinomial(t) for t, w in zip(types, weights)}


def demo_exchangeable() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("7.  Exchangeable classes: cheap however wild")
    print("=" * 78)
    print("    Theorem:  ANY permutation-invariant class on A^n has")
    print("              C_S <= (n+1)^(|A|-1),  price <= (|A|-1) log2(n+1).")
    print()
    rng = random.Random(31415)
    for n, m, n_sources in ((6, 2, 40), (8, 2, 60), (5, 3, 40)):
        sources = [random_exchangeable_source(n, m, rng) for _ in range(n_sources)]
        words = list(itertools.product(range(m), repeat=n))
        # sanity: each source is a probability distribution and is exchangeable
        for src in sources[:3]:
            mass = sum(src[word_type(w, m)] for w in words)
            assert abs(mass - 1.0) < 1e-9
        c_s = sum(max(src[word_type(w, m)] for src in sources) for w in words)
        price = math.log2(c_s)
        bound = (m - 1) * math.log2(n + 1)
        assert price <= bound + 1e-9
        print(
            f"    n={n:>2}, |A|={m}, {n_sources} random exchangeable sources:"
            f"  price = {price:.4f} bits  <=  bound {bound:.4f} bits"
        )
    print()
    print("    Even the class of ALL exchangeable laws is bounded the same way:")
    for n in (10, 100, 1000):
        print(f"        binary, n = {n:>4}:  price <= log2(n+1) = {math.log2(n + 1):.4f} bits")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8.  The NML code itself
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def nml_code_lengths(n: int, m: int) -> Dict[Tuple[int, ...], float]:
    """Code length (in bits) that the optimal universal code assigns to each
    type class of A^n for the memoryless class:
        -log2 maxlik(N) + log2 C_S   for one representative word of type N.
    """
    c_s = shtarkov_iid(n, m)
    lengths: Dict[Tuple[int, ...], float] = {}
    for counts in compositions(n, m):
        lengths[counts] = -math.log2(type_max_likelihood(counts)) + math.log2(c_s)
    return lengths


def demo_nml_code() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("8.  The optimal universal code (normalized maximum likelihood)")
    print("=" * 78)
    n, m = 12, 2
    lengths = nml_code_lengths(n, m)
    print(f"    binary messages of length n = {n};  price = {math.log2(shtarkov_iid(n, m)):.4f} bits")
    print()
    print(f"    {'type (#0,#1)':>14} {'-log2 maxlik':>14} {'NML length':>12} {'redundancy':>12}")
    for counts in sorted(lengths, reverse=True):
        maxlik = type_max_likelihood(counts)
        print(
            f"    {str(counts):>14} {-math.log2(maxlik):>14.4f} {lengths[counts]:>12.4f}"
            f" {lengths[counts] + math.log2(maxlik):>12.4f}"
        )
    print()
    print("    The redundancy column is CONSTANT: the NML code is exactly minimax,")
    print("    paying the same log2 C_S bits on every message and every source.")
    print()

    print()
    print("#" * 78)
    print("#  THE PRICE OF UNIVERSALITY -- numerical demonstrations")
    print("#" * 78)
    print()
    demo_iid_sandwich()
    demo_binary_leading_coefficient()
    demo_multiplicativity()
    demo_sharing_dichotomy()
    demo_model_selection()
    demo_finite_state()
    demo_exchangeable()
    demo_nml_code()
    print("All assertions passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Iterator, List, Sequence, Tuple


def compositions(n: int, m: int) -> Iterator[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    if m == 1:
        yield (n,)
        return
    for first in range(n + 1):
        for rest in compositions(n - first, m - 1):
            yield (first,) + rest


def multinomial(counts: Sequence[int]) -> int:
    total, value = sum(counts), math.factorial(sum(counts))
    for c in counts:
        value //= math.factorial(c)
    return value


def word_type(word: Sequence[int], m: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    counts = [0] * m
    for letter in word:
        counts[letter] += 1
    return tuple(counts)


def max_likelihood(counts: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """max_theta p_theta(x) for any word x of the given type."""
    n = sum(counts)
    value = 1.0
    for c in counts:
        if c > 0:
            value *= (c / n) ** c
    return value


def shtarkov_sum(n: int, m: int) -> float:
    return sum(multinomial(t) * max_likelihood(t) for t in compositions(n, m))


def type_index(counts: Tuple[int, ...], n: int, m: int) -> int:
    """Rank of a type in the lexicographic enumeration of all types."""
    return sorted(compositions(n, m)).index(tuple(counts))


def word_index_within_type(word: Sequence[int], m: int) -> int:
    """Combinatorial rank of a word among all words with the same letter counts.

    Standard enumerative ranking: scan left to right, and at each position add the
    number of words that would start with a smaller admissible letter.
    """
    counts = list(word_type(word, m))
    n = len(word)
    rank = 0
    for pos, letter in enumerate(word):
        remaining = n - pos - 1
        for smaller in range(letter):
            if counts[smaller] > 0:
                counts[smaller] -= 1
                rank += multinomial(counts) if remaining >= 0 else 0
                counts[smaller] += 1
        counts[letter] -= 1
    return rank


def nml_code_length_bits(word: Sequence[int], m: int) -> float:
    """The exact NML code length  -log2 maxlik(x) + log2 C_S."""
    n = len(word)
    counts = word_type(word, m)
    return -math.log2(max_likelihood(counts)) + math.log2(shtarkov_sum(n, m))


def encode(word: Sequence[int], m: int) -> Tuple[int, int, float]:
    """Return (type index, index within type, exact NML length in bits).

    The two integers are a lossless representation of the message; the enumerative
    code that writes them costs log2(#types) + log2(multinomial) bits, which is within
    an additive constant of the NML length.
    """
    n = len(word)
    counts = word_type(word, m)
    return type_index(counts, n, m), word_index_within_type(word, m), nml_code_length_bits(word, m)


def decode(t_index: int, w_index: int, n: int, m: int) -> List[int]:
    """Inverse of `encode`: reconstruct the message from its two indices."""
    counts = list(sorted(compositions(n, m))[t_index])
    word: List[int] = []
    for pos in range(n):
        for letter in range(m):
            if counts[letter] == 0:
                continue
            counts[letter] -= 1
            block = multinomial(counts)
            if w_index < block:
                word.append(letter)
                break
            w_index -= block
            counts[letter] += 1
    return word

def binary_price_log2(n: int) -> float:
    """log2 of the exact Shtarkov sum of the binary memoryless class on {0,1}^n."""
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0
    lf = math.lgamma(n + 1)
    terms: List[float] = []
    for j in range(n + 1):
        t = lf - math.lgamma(j + 1) - math.lgamma(n - j + 1)
        if j > 0:
            t += j * math.log(j / n)
        if n - j > 0:
            t += (n - j) * math.log((n - j) / n)
        terms.append(t)
    peak = max(terms)
    return (peak + math.log(sum(math.exp(x - peak) for x in terms))) / math.log(2.0)

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>The Price of Universality</h1>
  <p class="lede">
    One decompressor must serve every source in a class. The unavoidable overhead — the
    <em>minimax pointwise redundancy</em> — equals log<sub>2</sub> of the Shtarkov sum
    <code>C_S = Σ<sub>x</sub> max<sub>θ</sub> p<sub>θ</sub>(x)</code>.
    Explore how it behaves.
  </p>

  <div class="tabs">
    <div class="tab active" data-tab="price">1 · Price vs. message length</div>
    <div class="tab" data-tab="share">2 · Shared vs. independent parameters</div>
    <div class="tab" data-tab="nml">3 · The optimal universal code</div>
  </div>

  <!-- ================= TAB 1 ================= -->
  <div class="panel" id="tab-price">
    <h2>Exact price, and the bounds that bracket it</h2>
    <p class="note">
      For the memoryless class over an alphabet of <em>m</em> letters, the likelihood depends on a
      message only through its letter counts, so
      <code>C_S = Σ<sub>types</sub> (n choose N) Π<sub>a</sub> (N<sub>a</sub>/n)<sup>N<sub>a</sub></sup></code>.
      The curve below is that exact sum; the dashed lines are the proved bounds
      <code>log₂ m ≤ log₂ C_S ≤ (m−1) log₂(n+1)</code>,
      and the dotted line is the true asymptotic <code>((m−1)/2)·log₂ n + c</code>.
    </p>
    <div class="ctl">
      <label>alphabet size m = <span id="mval">2</span></label>
      <input type="range" id="m" min="2" max="4" step="1" value="2" />
    </div>
    <div class="ctl">
      <label>maximum message length n = <span id="nmaxval">48</span></label>
      <input type="range" id="nmax" min="8" max="60" step="1" value="48" />
    </div>
    <canvas id="c1" width="900" height="320"></canvas>
    <div class="legend">
      <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#6ee7ff"></span>exact price log₂ C_S</span>
      <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#ffd166"></span>type bound (m−1)log₂(n+1)</span>
      <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#ff7b9c"></span>packing bound log₂ m</span>
      <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#a3f7bf"></span>asymptotic ((m−1)/2)log₂ n + c</span>
    </div>
    <div class="readout" id="ro1"></div>
  </div>

  <!-- ================= TAB 2 ================= -->
  <div class="panel hidden" id="tab-share">
    <h2>The dichotomy: sharing a parameter is what makes universality cheap</h2>
    <p class="note">
      Same alphabet, same total number of symbols, same memorylessness — only the
      <em>parameter layout</em> differs. Left: <em>k</em> blocks of length <em>n</em>, each with its own
      unknown bias (price is exactly additive, <code>k · log₂ C_S(n)</code>). Right: one bias shared by all
      <em>kn</em> symbols (price <code>≈ ½ log₂(kn)</code>). The gap is the number of bits a
      specialized decompressor absorbs for free.
    </p>
    <div class="ctl">
      <label>block length n = <span id="blval">32</span></label>
      <input type="range" id="bl" min="4" max="64" step="1" value="32" />
    </div>
    <div class="ctl">
      <label>number of blocks k = <span id="kval">200</span></label>
      <input type="range" id="k" min="1" max="2000" step="1" value="200" />
    </div>
    <canvas id="c2" width="900" height="320"></canvas>
    <div class="legend">
      <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#ff7b9c"></span>independent parameters (linear in k)</span>
      <span><span class="swatch" style="background:#6ee7ff"></span>shared parameter (logarithmic in k)</span>
    </div>
    <div class="readout" id="ro2"></div>
  </div>

  <!-- ================= TAB 3 ================= -->
  <div class="panel hidden" id="tab-nml">
    <h2>The normalized maximum likelihood code, message by message</h2>
    <p class="note">
      The optimal universal code is <code>q*(x) = max<sub>θ</sub> p<sub>θ</sub>(x) / C_S</code>, giving length
      <code>−log₂ max<sub>θ</sub> p<sub>θ</sub>(x) + log₂ C_S</code>.
      Its redundancy against the best-fitting source is the <em>same</em> on every message — that
      flat last column is exactly what "minimax" means.
    </p>
    <div class="ctl">
      <label>binary message length n = <span id="n3val">12</span></label>
      <input type="range" id="n3" min="2" max="24" step="1" value="12" />
    </div>
    <div id="tbl"></div>
    <div class="readout" id="ro3"></div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
"use strict";

/* ---------- exact Shtarkov sums by the method of types ---------- */
const LGAMMA_C = [76.18009172947146,-86.50532032941677,24.01409824083091,
                  -1.231739572450155,0.1208650973866179e-2,-0.5395239384953e-5];
function lgamma(x){
  let y=x, tmp=x+5.5; tmp-=(x+0.5)*Math.log(tmp);
  let ser=1.000000000190015;
  for(let j=0;j<6;j++){ y+=1; ser+=LGAMMA_C[j]/y; }
  return -tmp+Math.log(2.5066282746310005*ser/x);
}
function logFact(n){ return lgamma(n+1); }

/* log2 of the exact Shtarkov sum of the i.i.d. class on A^n, |A| = m */
function priceIID(n, m){
  if(n===0) return 0;
  const terms=[];
  const counts=new Array(m).fill(0);
  (function rec(pos, left, logTerm){
    if(pos===m-1){
      const c=left;
      let t=logTerm-logFact(c)+(c>0? c*Math.log(c/n):0);
      terms.push(t);
      return;
    }
    for(let c=0;c<=left;c++){
      rec(pos+1,left-c,logTerm-logFact(c)+(c>0? c*Math.log(c/n):0));
    }
  })(0,n,logFact(n));
  const peak=Math.max(...terms);
  let s=0; for(const t of terms) s+=Math.exp(t-peak);
  return (peak+Math.log(s))/Math.LN2;
}
const priceCache=new Map();
function price(n,m){
  const key=n+"|"+m;
  if(!priceCache.has(key)) priceCache.set(key, priceIID(n,m));
  return priceCache.get(key);
}
/* asymptotic: ((m-1)/2) log2(n/2pi) + log2( pi^{m/2} / Gamma(m/2) ) */
function priceAsym(n,m){
  const ln=(m-1)/2*Math.log(n/(2*Math.PI)) + ((m/2)*Math.log(Math.PI)-lgamma(m/2));
  return ln/Math.LN2;
}
/* binary price for large n, in log space over j (O(n)) */
function priceBinary(n){
  if(n===0) return 0;
  const terms=[];
  const lf=logFact(n);
  for(let j=0;j<=n;j++){
    let t=lf-logFact(j)-logFact(n-j);
    if(j>0) t+=j*Math.log(j/n);
    if(n-j>0) t+=(n-j)*Math.log((n-j)/n);
    terms.push(t);
  }
  const peak=Math.max(...terms);
  let s=0; for(const t of terms) s+=Math.exp(t-peak);
  return (peak+Math.log(s))/Math.LN2;
}
const binCache=new Map();
function pb(n){ if(!binCache.has(n)) binCache.set(n, priceBinary(n)); return binCache.get(n); }

/* ---------- plotting helpers ---------- */
function setup(cv){
  const dpr=window.devicePixelRatio||1;
  const w=cv.clientWidth, h=cv.clientHeight;
  cv.width=w*dpr; cv.height=h*dpr;
  const g=cv.getContext("2d"); g.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0);
  g.clearRect(0,0,w,h);
  return {g,w,h};
}
function axes(g,w,h,xlab,ylab,x0,x1,y0,y1){
  const L=54,R=14,T=14,B=34;
  g.strokeStyle="#2a323d"; g.lineWidth=1; g.fillStyle="#94a3b8"; g.font="11px sans-serif";
  for(let i=0;i<=4;i++){
    const y=T+(h-T-B)*i/4;
    g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(L,y); g.lineTo(w-R,y); g.stroke();
    const v=y1-(y1-y0)*i/4;
    g.fillText(v.toFixed(1), 8, y+4);
  }
  for(let i=0;i<=5;i++){
    const x=L+(w-L-R)*i/5;
    const v=x0+(x1-x0)*i/5;
    g.fillText(v.toFixed(0), x-10, h-14);
  }
  g.fillText(xlab, (w-L-R)/2+L-20, h-2);
  g.save(); g.translate(12,(h)/2+20); g.rotate(-Math.PI/2); g.fillText(ylab,0,0); g.restore();
  return {L,R,T,B,
    X: v => L+(w-L-R)*(v-x0)/(x1-x0),
    Y: v => T+(h-T-B)*(1-(v-y0)/(y1-y0))};
}
function curve(g,pts,color,dash){
  g.strokeStyle=color; g.lineWidth=2; g.setLineDash(dash||[]);
  g.beginPath();
  pts.forEach((p,i)=> i? g.lineTo(p[0],p[1]) : g.moveTo(p[0],p[1]));
  g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);
}
function cards(id, items){
  document.getElementById(id).innerHTML = items.map(
    it => `<div class="card"><div class="k">${it[0]}</div><div class="v">${it[1]}</div></div>`
  ).join("");
}

/* ---------- tab 1 ---------- */
function drawPrice(){
  const m=+document.getElementById("m").value;
  const nmax=+document.getElementById("nmax").value;
  document.getElementById("mval").textContent=m;
  document.getElementById("nmaxval").textContent=nmax;
  const cv=document.getElementById("c1"); const {g,w,h}=setup(cv);
  const upper=(m-1)*Math.log2(nmax+1);
  const A=axes(g,w,h,"message length n","bits",1,nmax,0,Math.max(upper*1.08,1));
  const ex=[],ub=[],lb=[],as=[];
  for(let n=1;n<=nmax;n++){
    ex.push([A.X(n),A.Y(price(n,m))]);
    ub.push([A.X(n),A.Y((m-1)*Math.log2(n+1))]);
    lb.push([A.X(n),A.Y(Math.log2(m))]);
    as.push([A.X(n),A.Y(Math.max(priceAsym(n,m),0))]);
  }
  curve(g,ub,"#ffd166",[6,4]);
  curve(g,lb,"#ff7b9c",[6,4]);
  curve(g,as,"#a3f7bf",[2,3]);
  curve(g,ex,"#6ee7ff");
  const n=nmax;
  cards("ro1",[
    ["exact price at n="+n, price(n,m).toFixed(3)+" bits"],
    ["type bound", ((m-1)*Math.log2(n+1)).toFixed(3)+" bits"],
    ["packing bound", Math.log2(m).toFixed(3)+" bits"],
    ["price per symbol", (price(n,m)/n).toFixed(4)+" bits/sym"],
    ["parameter dimension", (m-1)],
    ["bound / exact", ((m-1)*Math.log2(n+1)/price(n,m)).toFixed(2)+"×"]
  ]);
}

/* ---------- tab 2 ---------- */
function drawShare(){
  const nb=+document.getElementById("bl").value;
  const k=+document.getElementById("k").value;
  document.getElementById("blval").textContent=nb;
  document.getElementById("kval").textContent=k;
  const cv=document.getElementById("c2"); const {g,w,h}=setup(cv);
  const per=pb(nb);
  const ymax=Math.max(per*k*1.08, 4);
  const A=axes(g,w,h,"number of blocks k","bits of universality",1,k,0,ymax);
  const ind=[],sh=[];
  const step=Math.max(1,Math.floor(k/300));
  for(let j=1;j<=k;j+=step){
    ind.push([A.X(j),A.Y(per*j)]);
    sh.push([A.X(j),A.Y(pb(j*nb))]);
  }
  curve(g,ind,"#ff7b9c");
  curve(g,sh,"#6ee7ff");
  const gap=per*k-pb(k*nb);
  cards("ro2",[
    ["price of one block", per.toFixed(3)+" bits"],
    ["independent (k blocks)", (per*k).toFixed(1)+" bits"],
    ["shared over "+(k*nb)+" symbols", pb(k*nb).toFixed(3)+" bits"],
    ["gap", gap.toFixed(1)+" bits"],
    ["gap per block", (gap/k).toFixed(3)+" bits"],
    ["proved floor (n=32,k≥5000)", (k>=5000?"k/4":"—")]
  ]);
}

/* ---------- tab 3 ---------- */
function drawNML(){
  const n=+document.getElementById("n3").value;
  document.getElementById("n3val").textContent=n;
  const CS=Math.pow(2,pb(n));
  let rows="<table><tr><th>type (#0,#1)</th><th>max likelihood</th><th>−log₂ maxlik</th><th>NML length</th><th>redundancy</th></tr>";
  for(let j=n;j>=0;j--){
    const p=j, q=n-j;
    let ml=1;
    if(p>0) ml*=Math.pow(p/n,p);
    if(q>0) ml*=Math.pow(q/n,q);
    const len=-Math.log2(ml)+Math.log2(CS);
    rows+=`<tr><td>(${q}, ${p})</td><td>${ml.toExponential(3)}</td><td>${(-Math.log2(ml)).toFixed(3)}</td><td>${len.toFixed(3)}</td><td>${(len+Math.log2(ml)).toFixed(3)}</td></tr>`;
  }
  rows+="</table>";
  document.getElementById("tbl").innerHTML=rows;
  cards("ro3",[
    ["Shtarkov sum C_S", CS.toFixed(4)],
    ["price log₂ C_S", pb(n).toFixed(4)+" bits"],
    ["number of types", (n+1)],
    ["type bound log₂(n+1)", Math.log2(n+1).toFixed(4)+" bits"]
  ]);
}

/* ---------- wiring ---------- */
document.querySelectorAll(".tab").forEach(t=>{
  t.addEventListener("click",()=>{
    document.querySelectorAll(".tab").forEach(o=>o.classList.remove("active"));
    t.classList.add("active");
    ["price","share","nml"].forEach(id=>{
      document.getElementById("tab-"+id).classList.toggle("hidden", id!==t.dataset.tab);
    });
    if(t.dataset.tab==="price") drawPrice();
    if(t.dataset.tab==="share") drawShare();
    if(t.dataset.tab==="nml") drawNML();
  });
});
["m","nmax"].forEach(id=>document.getElementById(id).addEventListener("input",drawPrice));
["bl","k"].forEach(id=>document.getElementById(id).addEventListener("input",drawShare));
document.getElementById("n3").addEventListener("input",drawNML);
window.addEventListener("resize",()=>{drawPrice();drawShare();});
drawPrice(); drawShare(); drawNML();
</script>

    distinguish two messages with the same letter counts. The <em>m<sup>n</sup></em> messages collapse into

<script>
"use strict";
function binom(n,k){ let r=1; for(let i=0;i<k;i++) r=r*(n-i)/(i+1); return Math.round(r); }
function factorial(n){ let r=1; for(let i=2;i<=n;i++) r*=i; return r; }

/* ---------------- section 1 ---------------- */
let word=[];
function newWord(){
  const n=+document.getElementById("n").value, m=+document.getElementById("m").value;
  word=Array.from({length:n},()=>Math.floor(Math.random()*m));
  render1();
}
function render1(){
  const n=+document.getElementById("n").value, m=+document.getElementById("m").value;
  document.getElementById("nv").textContent=n;
  document.getElementById("mv").textContent=m;
  if(word.length!==n || Math.max(...word)>=m) { word=Array.from({length:n},()=>Math.floor(Math.random()*m)); }
  const el=document.getElementById("word");

### A guided tour of how many bits a shared decompressor owes to everyone

---

## 0 · The question, in one paragraph

Every general-purpose compressor carries an invisible tax. The compressed file is short — that is the point — but the program that reads it is not specialized to *your* data. One decompressor serves spreadsheets, genomes, photographs and server logs alike, and readiness costs something: a few of the bits in your file are not describing your data at all, but telling a universal reader *where in the space of possibilities to look*.

This page is about pinning that tax down exactly. How many bits is it? What does it depend on? And — the practical question — is it ever worth building a decompressor specialized to one kind of data?

The punchline, which we will earn step by step:

> **Universality costs a logarithm of the message length when the data class has one shared parameter, and a linear number of bits when it has many independent ones. Bits move from the message into the decompressor at the rate of the parameter count, not the message length.**

---

## 1 · Codes are probability distributions in disguise

One translation makes the whole subject tractable.

A uniquely decodable binary code on a finite message set $\mathcal{X}$ has lengths $\ell(x)$ satisfying Kraft's inequality $\sum_x 2^{-\ell(x)} \le 1$; conversely any probability distribution $q$ gives a code with lengths $\approx -\log_2 q(x)$. So a **code is a probability distribution**, and we will identify the two.

If the data really came from a source $p$, the ideal code spends $-\log_2 p(x)$ bits; your scheme $q$ spends $-\log_2 q(x)$. The difference

$$R(q,p,x) \;=\; \log_2 \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$$

is the **redundancy** — the bits you wasted by not knowing $p$.

<details>
<summary><strong>Click for the details: why Kraft makes codes and distributions interchangeable</strong></summary>

Kraft's inequality says a prefix-free binary code with lengths $\ell(x)$ exists if and only if $\sum_x 2^{-\ell(x)}\le 1$. Given such a code, $q(x) = 2^{-\ell(x)}$ is a sub-probability, which we may normalize. Given a distribution $q$, the choice $\ell(x) = \lceil -\log_2 q(x)\rceil$ satisfies Kraft and loses at most one bit per message. Throughout, we drop the ceiling and work with idealized real-valued lengths; every statement below is therefore accurate to within one bit of any implementable scheme. See [Kraft's inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraft%E2%80%93McMillan_inequality) for the classical statement.
</details>

---

## 2 · The one formula that starts everything

You do not know $p$. You know only that it belongs to a **source class** $\{p_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta}$ — all biased coins, say, or all Markov chains on a given alphabet. You must fix one code $q$ in advance and live with it, for every source and every message. The natural target is the worst case:

$$\mathcal{R} \;=\; \min_q\ \max_x\ \max_\theta\ \log_2\frac{p_\theta(x)}{q(x)}.$$

This *minimax pointwise redundancy* is the **price of universality**, and it has an exact closed form. Define the **Shtarkov sum**

$$C_S \;=\; \sum_{x} \max_\theta\, p_\theta(x)$$

— for each message, the best explanation any source in the class can offer, summed over all messages. Then

$$\mathcal{R} \;=\; \log_2 C_S,$$

achieved by the **normalized maximum likelihood** code $q^*(x)= \max_\theta p_\theta(x)/C_S$.

<details>
<summary><strong>Click to reveal the proof (it is four lines)</strong></summary>

*Upper bound.* $q^*$ is a probability distribution by construction. For every $\theta$ and $x$,
$$\log_2\frac{p_\theta(x)}{q^*(x)} = \log_2\frac{p_\theta(x)\,C_S}{\max_{\theta'}p_{\theta'}(x)} \le \log_2 C_S,$$
with equality at the maximizing $\theta$. So $q^*$ pays exactly $\log_2 C_S$, uniformly.

*Lower bound.* Suppose some $q$ had worst-case redundancy $< \log_2 C_S$. Then $q(x) > \max_\theta p_\theta(x)/C_S$ for every $x$; summing over $\mathcal{X}$ gives $1 = \sum_x q(x) > 1$, a contradiction. $\blacksquare$

Two immediate corollaries. First, $C_S \ge 1$ (take any single source and sum its probabilities), so **the price is never negative** — universality never helps. Second, the entire problem is now the evaluation of one scalar.
</details>

## 3 · Counting types: why the price is logarithmic

Take the **memoryless class**: messages of length $n$ over an $m$-letter alphabet, each letter drawn independently from an unknown probability vector $\theta$. Its likelihood regroups as

$$p_\theta(x) \;=\; \prod_{j=1}^n \theta_{x_j} \;=\; \prod_{a} \theta_a^{N_a(x)},$$

where $N_a(x)$ counts occurrences of the letter $a$. So the likelihood — *for every source at once* — depends on the message only through the vector of counts $N(x)$, its **type**.

That is decisive, because types are few: each count lies in $\{0,\dots,n\}$ and they sum to $n$, so there are at most $(n+1)^{m-1}$ of them. Grouping the Shtarkov sum by type, each type contributes at most $1$, and

$$C_S \le (n+1)^{m-1}, \qquad \mathcal{R} \le (m-1)\log_2(n+1)\ \text{bits}.$$

The exponent $m-1$ is exactly the **dimension of the parameter space** — one less than the alphabet size, because probabilities sum to one.

<details>
<summary><strong>Click for the general principle: any sufficient statistic bounds the price</strong></summary>

**Lemma.** If $T:\mathcal{X}\to\Sigma$ is any map into a finite set such that $T(x)=T(y)$ implies $p_\theta(x)=p_\theta(y)$ for every $\theta$, then $C_S \le |\Sigma|$.

*Proof.* Partition $\mathcal{X}$ into the fibers of $T$. On a fiber $F$ the maximum likelihood is a constant $v_F$, and for a source nearly attaining it, $|F|\,v_F \le \sum_{x\in F}p_\theta(x)\le 1$. So each fiber contributes $|F|v_F\le1$, and there are at most $|\Sigma|$ fibers. $\blacksquare$

The entire [method of types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Method_of_types) is this lemma with $T$ the count vector. We will use it three more times below: for finite-state sources with the (state, letter) counts, and for exchangeable classes with the counts again.
</details>

## 5 · The price is real, and it multiplies

An upper bound alone proves nothing: maybe the price is zero and there is nothing to save. It is not zero.

**Packing.** If you can find distinct messages $x_1,\dots,x_N$ and sources $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N$ with $p_{\theta_i}$ putting mass on $x_i$, then $\sum_i p_{\theta_i}(x_i) \le C_S$, because each term is one of the terms of the defining sum. Applied to the $m$ *deterministic* sources on the $m$ constant messages $aaa\cdots a$: $C_S\ge m$, so $\mathcal{R}\ge \log_2 m$ for every $n$. Small, but it never goes away.

{{algorithm:2}}

**Multiplication.** Now the structural fact. For two classes composed independently — messages are pairs $(x,y)$, sources are pairs acting independently — the maximum likelihood factorizes, and therefore

$$C_S(\mathcal{S}\otimes\mathcal{T}) = C_S(\mathcal{S})\cdot C_S(\mathcal{T}), \qquad C_S(\mathcal{S}^{\otimes k}) = C_S(\mathcal{S})^k.$$

Exactly — not an inequality. **The price of universality is additive over independently parameterized blocks.**

<details>
<summary><strong>Click for the subtle step: proving the factorization without compactness</strong></summary>

The obvious direction, $\max_{(\theta,\psi)}p_\theta(x)p_\psi(y) \le (\max_\theta p_\theta(x))(\max_\psi p_\psi(y))$, is monotonicity. The reverse needs care, because the parameter set is typically an infinite simplex and the supremum need not be attained, so one cannot simply "pick the maximizers".

The device that replaces compactness is a *division trick*:

> If $c\ge0$ and $c\,p_\theta(x) \le P$ for every $\theta$, then $c\,\widehat p(x)\le P$, where $\widehat p = \sup_\theta p_\theta$.

(If $c=0$ this is trivial; if $c>0$, divide, take the supremum, multiply back.) Apply it twice. Writing $P$ for the maximum likelihood of the pair, first fix $\theta$ and run the trick over $\psi$ with $c=p_\theta(x)$, obtaining $p_\theta(x)\widehat p(y)\le P$; then run it over $\theta$ with $c = \widehat p(y)$, obtaining $\widehat p(y)\widehat p(x)\le P$. $\blacksquare$

The same one-coordinate-at-a-time argument, iterated over a growing set of already-maximized coordinates, gives the $k$-fold version.
</details>
